title: स्थानीय पाठ्यक्रमको कार्यान्वयनको अवस्था {Status of local curriculum implementation}
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेख स्थानीय पाठ्यक्रमको कार्यान्वयनको अवस्था, पाठ्यक्रमको आवश्यकता, प्रभावकारिता, कार्यान्वयनमा देखिएका समस्या र समाधानका उपायहरू प्रस्तुत गर्ने उद्देश्यले अध्ययन गरिएको छ । इलाम जिल्ला फाकफोकथुम गाउँपालिकाअन्तर्गत चारवटा सामुदायिक विद्यालयका प्रधानाध्यापकहरू, स्थानीय पाठ्यक्रम विषय अध्यापन गर्ने शिक्षकहरू, शिक्षाशाखा प्रमुख र १० जना विद्यार्थीहरूलाई नमुनाको रूपमा छनोट गरिएको छ । प्रधानाध्यापक, शिक्षक र शिक्षाशाखा प्रमुख तथा साविकका स्रोत ब्यक्तिलाई अन्तर्वार्ता, प्रश्नावली, विद्यार्थीहरूसँग छलफल तथा कक्षाकोठा अवलोकन गरी आएका कुराहरूलाई तथ्याङ्कको रूपमा समावेश गरिएको छ । प्राप्त तथ्याङ्कको वर्णनात्मक ढाँचामा ब्याख्या तथा विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । अध्ययनको क्रममा प्राप्त सूचनालाई विश्लेषण गर्दा छनौटमा परेका विद्यालयहरूमा स्थानीय विषयका रूपमा मातृभाषा र अंग्रेजी तथा कम्प्युटर विषय समेटेर स्थानीय पाठ्यक्रमको रूपमा पढाइ भइरहेको र सो विषय शिक्षण गर्न छुट्टै विषय शिक्षकको कमी रहेको पाइयो । स्थानीय विषय छनोट गर्दा शिक्षाशाखा प्रमुखको सल्लाह बमोजिम प्रधानाध्यापक ,शिक्षकहरू, अभिभावकहरू, र स्थानीय नेतृत्व संलग्न रहेको पाइयो । स्थानीय विषय शिक्षण गर्ने क्रममा शैक्षिक सामग्रीको प्रयोगको अवस्था र उपलब्धता सन्तोषजनक नरहेको, स्थानीय विषय शिक्षणको अनुगमन तथा मूल्याङ्ककन प्रधानाध्यापकले एक वा दुई महिनामा एक पटक गर्ने गरेको पाइयो । छनौटमा परेको विद्यालयहरूले हालको मूल्याङ्कन प्रणालीहरूलाई भन्दा परम्परागत मूल्याङ्कन प्रणालीलाई प्रयोगमा ल्याएको, स्थानीय विषय शिक्षणको लागि स्थानीय विषय पढाउन शिक्षकलाई आवश्यक तालिम तथा सेवा सुविधाको व्यवस्था नभएको साथै शिक्षण सिकाई प्रक्रिया प्रभावकारी हुन नसकेकोले यसको कार्यान्वयनमा सवै सरोकारवाला निकायहरूको ध्यान जान आवश्यक छ ।
american_english: The present article has been studied with the objective of presenting the status of implementation of the local curriculum, the need for the curriculum, its effectiveness, the problems seen in implementation and the measures for their solution. Four community schools under Phakphokthum Rural Municipality in Ilam district were selected as samples, along with the principals, teachers who teach local curriculum subjects, the head of the education section and 10 students. The principals, teachers and head of the education section, along with former resource persons, were given interviews, questionnaires, discussions with students and classroom observation, and the matters arising were included as data. The obtained data were interpreted and analyzed in a descriptive format. While analyzing the information obtained during the study, it was found that in the selected schools local subjects such as mother tongue, English and computer were being taught as the local curriculum, and that there was a shortage of separate subject teachers to teach that subject. It was found that when selecting local subjects, the principal, teachers, guardians and local leadership were involved in accordance with the advice of the head of the education section. It was found that the state of use and availability of educational materials during the teaching of local subjects was not satisfactory, and that monitoring and evaluation of local subject teaching was done by the principal once in one or two months. The selected schools were found to have used the traditional assessment system rather than the present assessment systems; necessary training and service facilities were not arranged for teachers to teach local subjects; and since the teaching-learning process could not be made effective, attention of all stakeholders is necessary in its implementation.

informal_english: This article looks at how the local curriculum is being put into practice, why it's needed, how well it works, what problems come up in putting it into practice and how to sort them out. Four community schools under Phakphokthum Rural Municipality in Ilam district were picked as samples, along with the heads, teachers who teach local curriculum subjects, the head of the education section and 10 students. The heads, teachers and head of the education section, plus former resource persons, were interviewed, given questionnaires, had discussions with students and classroom observations, and what came out of all that was taken as data. The data were then picked apart in a descriptive format. Looking through the information gathered during the study, it turned out that in the chosen schools local subjects like mother tongue, English and computer were being taught as the local curriculum, and there weren't enough separate subject teachers to teach them. When picking local subjects, the head, teachers, parents and local leaders were involved following the advice of the head of the education section. The use and availability of teaching materials for local subjects wasn't up to scratch, and monitoring and evaluation of local subject teaching was done by the head once every month or two. The chosen schools were found to have used the old-style assessment system rather than the current ones; the necessary training and service facilities weren't in place for teachers teaching local subjects; and since the teaching and learning process couldn't be made effective, everyone involved really needs to pay attention to how it's implemented.
